title: Recarbonization of Global Soils (RECSOIL) - Legume Cover Cropping Framework
source: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
summary: Introduction of multi-species legume-based cover crops (e.g., Vicia villosa, Trifolium repens, Crotalaria juncea) in depleted croplands (SOC < 0.5%). Root exudates stimulate mycorrhizal fungi and increase aggregate stability.

quantified_impact.soil_organic_carbon_increase_pct: 15-25% over 2-3 years (0.2-0.5 t C/ha/year sequestration rate)

scientific_mechanism: Legumes synthesize atmospheric N2 into bioavailable ammonium via rhizobial symbiosis. The resulting low C:N ratio biomass decomposes into microbial residues (necromass), which chemically bond with mineral silt and clay fractions to form stable micro-aggregates, permanently locking organic carbon in the soil profile.
recommended_interventions: Plant multi-species legume cover crops during fallow or inter-row cycles
Terminate mechanically through roller-crimping rather than glyphosate to preserve fungal hyphae
Maintain minimum 30% surface residue cover year-round

title: Conservation Agriculture: Minimum Soil Disturbance and Biological Soil Tillage
source: FAO Global Soil Partnership & ICAR Technical Bulletin
summary: Zero-tillage combined with organic retention curtails oxidation of humus and disruption of earthworm (Lumbricidae) burrows in intensive grain systems.

quantified_impact.fuel_and_emissions_reduction: 30-40% drop in on-farm tractor diesel consumption

scientific_mechanism: Inverting soil through deep disc ploughing exposes internal aggregates to UV radiation and rapid microbial oxidation, volatilizing carbon as CO2. Direct drilling preserves mycorrhizal networks and promotes earthworm endogeic populations.
recommended_interventions: Transition from deep inversion tillage to direct no-till seeders
Retain at least 2.5 tonnes/ha of crop residue on topsoil
Introduce brassica deep-root bio-drills (Daikon radish) to alleviate subsoil compaction without steel
